tfn.s: The study suggests that total time spent on a phone is the main factor behind the slowdown.
tfn.why: The effect varied with relevance and habit, "rather than simply the total amount of time spent using a device".

tfn.s: A notification can compete with a task even when its content turns out to be irrelevant.
tfn.why: We assess a message's significance only after turning our attention to it, and "that repeated appraisal competes" with the task.

speak.title: Role-play: the ten-minute reply rule
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You want your team to answer work messages within ten minutes, even in the evening. Explain why. Ask at least two questions, then decide: agree a rule, change it, or keep it.

b.text: You want to switch off work alerts after six o'clock because you can't concentrate or rest. Explain how it affects you and suggest a rule that works for both of you.

phrases: I'd like to switch off alerts after six.
I can't concentrate when my phone keeps buzzing.
We're a small team, so I need quick answers.
Could we agree a time to reply?
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: what rule did you agree, and is it fair for both people?
